# MacroMag OS

> MacroMag OS is an open-source, zero-telemetry Linux distribution written from the ground up in Rust and C, featuring a stripped-down Linux kernel and the Virtualized Object Shell (VOS).

## Overview
- **Project Name:** MacroMag OS (MacroMag-32)
- **Category:** Linux Distribution / Operating System
- **Creator:** Adrian Morawski (initiated in 2025/2026)
- **License:** GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPL v3)
- **Architecture:** x86_64
- **Primary Languages:** Rust
- **Mission:** Fighting planned obsolescence and e-waste by giving older x86_64 hardware a second life with zero background telemetry and no legacy GNU clutter.

## Core Components
- **Virtualized Object Shell (VOS):** A strongly-typed, object-oriented PID 1 init runtime and shell written in Rust (~400 KB static binary). Replaces traditional raw-text POSIX pipelines (`grep`, `awk`, `sed`) with typed in-memory object pipelines (e.g., `sys.ps() | where memory > 256MB | select pid, name`) and built-in Linux namespace sandboxing (`sandbox(net: false) ->`).
- **MUR (MacroMag User Repository):** A lightweight, git-free package manager written in Rust that syncs packages and verifies SHA-256 checksums without heavy dependencies.
- **Stripped-Down Linux Kernel:** Uses the Linux kernel purely as a deterministic hardware abstraction layer without bloated userland daemons.
